citation: Portes, P. R., González Canché, M., Boada, D., & Whatley, M. E. (2018). Early evaluation findings from the Instructional Conversation study: Culturally responsive teaching outcomes for diverse learners in elementary school. American Educational Research Journal, 55(3), 488–531. https://doi.org/10.3102/0002831217741089
report_number: AERJ 55(3):488-531; DOI 10.3102/0002831217741089 (efficacy RCT from IES grant R305A100670, 'Improving the Teaching and Learning of English Language Learners: The Instructional Conversational Model', Univ. of Georgia)
design: Cluster RCT; assignment level = teacher/class. 82 teachers randomized in 2 cohorts; 74 retained (40 treatment / 34 control) across 22 schools, 14 districts in a southeastern US state; 11% teacher attrition (1.77% differential, below WWC conservative cutoff). N=1,521 consented students (third + fifth grade; ~746 non-ELL / ~764 ELL after W-APT adjustment). Intervention = Instructional Conversation (IC) pedagogy professional development (100-hour assisted-teaching program + a 'practice' year, then 1 efficacy year of small-group IC instruction 1-2x/week, ~30 min). Comparison = business-as-usual control teachers. Outcomes = state Criterion-Referenced Competency Tests (CRCT) in ELA, reading, math, science, social studies, standardized to z-scores within grade x content area; immediate end-of-efficacy-year post-test. Analysis = OLS (treatment, gender, grade, interactions); pretest covariate available only for fifth graders (Table 14).
problems: (1) Reporting structure limits clean full-sample TPD-vs-control contrasts. The randomized full sample (all students, ELLs + non-ELLs) is analysed for ONLY ONE achievement subject: ELA (Table 8). The article's Hypothesis 1 (confirmatory) concerns ELA for the combined sample. Reading, math, science, and social-studies treatment effects are reported ONLY for the ELL sample (Tables 9-13), which the authors themselves state is NON-randomised in effect: teacher-level randomization did NOT achieve baseline equivalence for ELLs (Table 5: fifth-grade ELL treatment students started significantly ahead in ALL subjects, d ~0.26-0.42), so the authors label the ELL results 'quasi-experimental and of heuristic value.' These ELL rows are therefore extracted as outcome_role=subgroup, is_full_sample=false. (2) Outcomes are z-standardized within grade x content area, so the OLS treatment coefficient on the z-scored outcome IS the standardized mean difference (Cohen's d); J small-sample correction ~1.0 (N=748-1,476). I use the treatment-only model (Model 1) coefficient as the unadjusted average treatment effect and its SE as impact_se; g = J*coef, g_se = J*SE. (3) These are SINGLE-LEVEL OLS estimates that do NOT account for the teacher-level clustering -> cluster_adjusted=false. n_clusters=74 teachers recorded for central cluster-correction (Hedges 2007). NO ICC is reported anywhere in the paper, so icc is left null (spec: never guess an ICC). (4) For full-sample ELA the article's headline figure is b=0.28 (p<.01) but that is the Model 4/5 INTERACTION-model coefficient = the conditional effect for fifth-grade non-female students, NOT the average treatment effect; the average treatment effect (Model 1, treatment-only) is 0.12 (p<.05), which I extract as the primary g and note the 0.28 conditional value. (5) These are mostly NOT pretest-adjusted (no pretest for third graders). Table 14 gives pretest-adjusted estimates but ONLY for fifth-grade ELLs (a further non-randomized subgroup, n~325-331): ELA 0.24** (g~0.24), Math -0.05, Science 0.07, Social Studies -0.11 -- these are noted in the relevant ELL records' notes, not added as separate rows. (6) PUBLICATION ERROR: Table 12 (Science, ELLs) is printed identically to Table 11 (Math, ELLs) -- same intercepts, treatment coefficients (0.15*/0.15/0.15/0.20), SEs, R2, N=753, RMSE. The narrative confirms Cohen's d=0.20 for both math and science (ELLs only) but the duplicated table means the Science treatment-only coefficient cannot be independently verified; recorded as 0.15 (=printed Table 12 Model 1) with this caveat. (7) Per-arm n_t/n_c left null for ELL rows (Table 7 per-cell counts not cleanly recoverable); for the full-sample ELA row approximate arm sizes from Table 3 consent counts (treatment 835, control 686 students) are recorded with a note (model N=1,476). (8) Subject mapping per spec: ELA/reading -> Reading; math/science -> STEM; social studies -> Other.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Instructional Conversation (IC) PD (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: State Criterion-Referenced Competency Test (CRCT) - English Language Arts
effect_sizes.g_method: OLS treatment coefficient (Table 8, Model 1, treatment-only) on grade-x-subject z-standardized CRCT-ELA = standardized mean difference d=0.12 (SE 0.05). g = J*d with J=0.99949 (df=N-2, N=1,476); g_se = J*SE; g_var = g_se^2. Standardized by the within-grade z-score SD (=1 by construction).
effect_sizes.notes: FULL randomized sample (all students, ELLs + non-ELLs). This is the report's confirmatory Hypothesis 1 outcome (ELA for combined sample). Article headline b=0.28** is the Model 4/5 interaction-model coefficient (conditional effect for fifth-grade non-female students), NOT the average treatment effect; Model 1 (0.12*, p<.05) is the average treatment effect and is extracted here. n_t/n_c approximate from Table 3 consent counts (treatment 835, control 686 students); model N observations = 1,476. OLS, single-level (not cluster-adjusted); 74 teacher clusters; no ICC reported. ELA -> Reading per spec. Math/science/social studies are NOT analysed for the full sample in this report (only for the ELL subgroup, see subgroup rows).
